{{Short description|Russian mathematician (born 1954)}}
'''Vladimir Georgievich Turaev''' (Владимир Георгиевич Тураев, born in 1954) is a Russian mathematician, specializing in topology.

Turaev received in 1979 from the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] his Candidate of Sciences degree (PhD) under [[Oleg Viro]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=56929}}</ref> Turaev was a professor at the [[University of Strasbourg]] and then became a professor at  [[Indiana University]]. In 2016, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].

Turaev's research deals with low-dimensional topology, quantum topology, and knot theory and their interconnections with quantum field theory. In 1991, [[Nicolai Reshetikhin|Reshetikhin]] and Turaev published a mathematical construction of new topological invariants of compact oriented 3-manifolds and framed links in these manifolds, corresponding to a mathematical implementation of ideas in quantum field theory published by [[Edward Witten|Witten]];<ref>{{cite journal|author=Reshetikhin, N.|author2=Turaev, V. G.|title=Invariants of 3-manifolds via link polynomials and quantum groups|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=103|issue=3|year=1991|pages=547–597|doi=10.1007/BF01239527|url=http://eudml.org/doc/143870|bibcode=1991InMat.103..547R|s2cid=123376541|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the invariants are now called Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev (or Reshetikhin-Turaev) invariants. In 1992, Turaev and Viro introduced a new family of invariants for 3-manifolds by using state sums computed on triangulations of manifolds;<ref>{{cite journal|author=Turaev, V. G.|author2=Viro, O. Y.|title=State sum invariants of 3-manifolds and quantum 6j-symbols|journal=Topology|volume=31|issue=4|year=1992|pages=865–902|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(92)90015-A|doi-access=}}</ref> these invariants are now called Turaev-Viro invariants.

In 1990, Turaev was an Invited Speaker with talk ''State sum models in low dimensional topology'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in [[Kyōto]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Turaev, Vladimir G.|chapter=State sum models in low-dimensional topology|title=Proc. ICM Kyoto|volume=1|pages=689–698|year=1990|chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265451900}}</ref> In 2016, he shared, with Alexis Virelizier, the Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize for their monograph ''Monoidal categories and topological field theory''.
